★ THE RULES OF THE STREET ★

Learn to Play

WAIT — Keep your iron holstered till the bell rings and you hear DRAW! Grab for it early and it's a foul.

DRAW — The instant it rings, press and HOLD on the street (hold your touch / mouse, or hold Space) — just hold, like the scope button in a mobile shooter. No sliding, no swiping, and no on-screen fire button: holding alone snaps your revolver straight up out of the leather into aim-down-sights, and the view tightens as the sights come up.

AIM — Aim with the iron itself. Keep holding to stay scoped in, and move or drag to swing the whole revolver until its front sight sits on a gunman. There is no floating crosshair — the gun is your aim.

SHOOT — RELEASE to fire once your sights are on him. Let go before the sights finish rising and it sprays wild from the hip. Head or heart kills outright, other hits wound — and the iron stays up in ADS for follow-up shots, no re-holstering till the duel is done.

RELOAD — Reloading is in your hands only: the iron never reloads itself. When you're low or empty, tap the round RELOAD button (bottom right) or press R any time the iron isn't full — even after a duel. Low guns load fast to make up for holding so little: a double barrel speed-loads both shells at once, in one hand motion, and a single-shot drops its one round straight in — while six-guns and lever rifles still feed one round at a time, so the big magazines take the longest to fill.

OUTNUMBERED — From Duel 4 on, they come in company: two gunmen at once in Duels 4 and 5, and three at once in the final duel. Every one of them draws and shoots on his own — drop them all to clear the street.

RANGE — Every duel is fought at a longer distance than the last, from 7 paces out to a 19-pace rifle shot.

SWITCH GUNS — In a duel you can switch guns at any time, same as on the ride: tap the 1 · REVOLVER / 2 · SHOTGUN / 3 · RIFLE buttons or press 1, 2, 3. Only guns you own can be drawn, and every gun keeps its own loads, draw speed, recoil, sway, aim zoom and range — so when a duel stretches out past a shotgun's reach, switch to your rifle or revolver and finish it.

LAN DUEL — Off the main menu: a 1v1 duel against a real person on a second phone on the same Wi-Fi. One player taps Create a Room and gets a 6-digit code; the other types that code and taps Join. Before the bell, either player can set the duel range — Near (7–9 paces), Midrange (11–13.5) or Long (16–19) — and it updates on both phones at once; when the duel starts, the exact paces are drawn from that range. Weapons update in real time — switch or equip a revolver, shotgun or rifle and your rival sees the new gun, in name and in hand, and duels against its real draw, recoil, sway, zoom, range damage and spread. The duel itself is the real thing: wait for the bell / DRAW!, early iron is a foul, head or heart kills outright, other hits wound, and your draw is timed to the millisecond — winner and loser decided on both phones at once.

SURVIVE — If they beat you to it, their lead costs you half your hide. Two hits and you're planted.

LONG GUNS & HATS — The Store also sells shotguns and rifles. A shotgun holds 2 shells and throws a pattern that starts tight and spreads wider the farther it flies — deadly up close, wild at range. Rifles hold more rounds and shoot straighter and harder. A long gun is carried in both hands, left hand on the fore-end — there is no holster for it, and its action needs working between shots. Know the balance of the street: a revolver draws fastest and bites hardest up close, but its lead fades at long range; a rifle draws slow, stays steadiest in the sights and hits harder the farther out the shot flies; a shotgun is slowest to shoulder, and its pattern spreads wider the farther it flies — tight and devastating up close, still heavy at mid range, and only at the longest ranges do most pellets miss and those that land land weaker. Hats from the Store are worn on your head in the cinematic and the duel, same as your coat. Everything you own lives in the Inventory — its own screen off the main menu, sorted into Guns, Hats and Clothes, with one-tap equip.

PRACTICE — No bell, no gunman. Twelve big, bright glass bottles stand on rails, barrels, crates and tables — in different spots every round, never the same layout twice — hold to aim down sights, release to shoot, and watch them shatter — and a shotgun's pattern breaks every bottle standing in its spread, not just the one you aimed at. Line a shot up dead through one bottle and the bullet carries straight on and breaks the bottle right behind it too — with any gun you hold. Your count is kept on screen — and the clock starts on your first shot, so clear them fast: your best time is saved and shown in Practice.

FLYING BOTTLES — The second practice, off the same menu: fifteen bottles are launched across the sky in front of you, big and close, tumbling end over end through midair on a long, slow arc at different heights and speeds — you get a good few seconds to track each one. Lead them, hold to aim, release to shoot — smash one and it bursts into flying glass with a shattering crack. A bottle that gets past you smashes on the ground and is gone. Your hits, the bottles still in the air and your shots are all counted on screen.

SCOPE — Rifles carry a 2× scope. The scope icon rides in your plate while a rifle is in hand, and when you hold to aim the scope settles over your aim point and the view doubles in — double, not too much — with its crosshairs dead on where you're pointing: the shot goes exactly where the scope points. While you're scoped, RELOAD stays pressable, and the EXIT SCOPE button (bottom left) drops you back out to normal view without firing — hold to aim again and the scope comes back. While the scope is up, its aim point sits above your fingertip, so your finger never covers the man you're aiming at — and the shot still goes exactly where the scope points.

THE RIDE — Saddle up off the main menu and run down a stagecoach on the open trail. Your horse gallops under you and the long coach bounces and swerves ahead on its team, and the six outlaws riding it — driver and messenger on the bench, two on the roof and two on the rear platform — shoot back. A man you drop ragdolls down off the coach and into the road behind it. Hold to aim, release to fire, same as a duel, and the coach body honestly blocks any shot that hits it instead of a man. Switch guns at any time: tap the REVOLVER / SHOTGUN / RIFLE buttons or press 1, 2, 3 — every gun keeps its own loads, and a gun you don't own can't be drawn, so buy shotguns and rifles in the Store first. Drop all six outlaws to take the coach and its $150 strongbox. Shooting a team horse slows the coach down; let it pull 30 paces ahead and it's gone — and their lead costs you a fifth of your hide a hit. Or pick ENDLESS when you ride: the coaches keep coming, each one different and harder — more outlaws, a faster coach, return fire that lands harder and truer — and the run only ends when your hide does. Your longest survive is kept in Settings.

SETTINGS — From the main menu, open Settings to turn the western background music on or off, to pick the frame rate — 30, 60 or 120 FPS — and to pick the graphics quality: Low, Medium or High. Low is the classic look; Medium renders sharper with soft shadows that follow the action; High renders the street at its finest, with rich golden light and dust hanging in the air. The game runs at the rate you pick, and your choices are kept between visits.

STATS — Your records live in Stats, off the main menu: your average and best draw, your shooting accuracy, and your fastest bottle clear with a revolver, a rifle and a shotgun — each weapon family keeps its own record, and all of them are kept between visits.

★ GAME UPDATES ★

What's New

Every update, in short — newest first.

v1.26 — Duel ranges in the LAN room. Pick a range instead of exact paces: Near (7–9 paces), Midrange (11–13.5) or Long (16–19). Either player sets it, both phones update at once, and the duel starts at a distance drawn from that range.

v1.25 — LAN Duel · 1v1. Face a real gunslinger on another phone, same Wi-Fi: one player creates a room and shares its 6-digit code, the other joins with it. Pick your duel distance together, watch each other's weapons update live as you switch and equip, then duel head-to-head under the normal rules — bell, fouls, head or heart — with a win or a loss for both phones.

v1.24 — Endless Stagecoach. Pressing Ride now asks first: Quick Run — the classic single chase for its $150 strongbox — or Endless: stagecoach after stagecoach, each one different and harder, with more outlaws aboard, a faster coach and guns shooting back harder and truer, until your hide runs out. Your longest survive time is saved and shown in Settings and on the Stagecoach screen. Also: your gunfighter now turns his body toward whatever he's aiming at — his stance swings with his aim in duels and on the ride, not just his gun.

v1.23 — Gun switching comes to duels. Swap between your revolver, shotgun and rifle at any time in a duel — the 1 · 2 · 3 buttons or keys, same as the stagecoach ride — using only the guns you own, each keeping its own loads, draw, recoil, sway, zoom and range. A shotgun alone can't finish a long duel: switch to rifle or revolver when the distance opens up. Also: while the rifle scope is up, its aim point now rides above your fingertip, so your finger never covers the target.

v1.22 — The game has a new name: Showdown 1881. It rides the title screen in carved gold western lettering, with the year set like a badge between brass rules — and the splash and HUD carry the new name too. New home-screen badge as well: a revolver crossed with a gold sheriff star against the sunset. Also in this build: Your Hide rides higher on screen, rifles stay in normal view until you hold to aim — no more auto-zoom — and Stagecoach now sits above Practice in the menu.

v1.21 — Decluttered: the ride and both practices run a lean HUD, and while the rifle scope is up everything non-essential shrinks or steps away — no duplicate scope label, no banner across the coach, messages short and quick to fade, and EXIT SCOPE never covers another button. Flying bottles fly closer and bigger too — same slow arc, far easier to see and hit. And the menu's two practice buttons are now one Practice button that asks first: Shooting Bottles or Flying Bottles.

v1.20 — The stagecoach chase grows: a longer coach carrying six outlaws, dead men ragdoll down into the road instead of standing stuck, and the ride's words and buttons sit clear of everything — nothing covers them, not even the rifle scope.

v1.19 — RELOAD stays pressable while you're looking through the rifle scope — and a new EXIT SCOPE button (bottom left, while scoped) drops you back out of the scope to normal view without firing.

v1.18 — Rifles get a scope: the scope icon shows while a rifle is in hand, aiming settles the lens over your aim point with a clean 2× zoom — double, not too much — and the shot goes exactly where the scope points.

v1.17 — New Ride mode: chase a stagecoach on horseback — a galloping horse, a bouncing, swerving coach on a team of horses, and three outlaws shooting back — and switch between revolver, shotgun and rifle at any time mid-ride.

v1.16 — The Store shows its goods: every gun, hat and outfit now carries a picture of the piece itself in its true colours and finish, so you see exactly what you're buying — and the shelves are laid out clean and tidy.

v1.15 — Collateral bottles: line a shot up dead through one bottle and the bullet carries on and breaks the bottle right behind it too — revolver, rifle and shotgun alike.

v1.14 — Shotguns and rifles are separate tabs now: the Store and your Inventory each give them their own tab, so the Shotguns tab shows only shotguns and the Rifles tab shows only rifles.

v1.13.1 — Flying bottles now launch from further out, on a longer, slower arc — a good few seconds in the air to track and lead, instead of whipping past.

v1.13 — New Flying Bottles practice: bottles are launched across the sky, tumbling through midair — smash them before they land, in a burst of glass shards with a real shattering crack and tinkle.

v1.12 — New Stats screen off the main menu: your average and best draw, your shooting accuracy, and your fastest bottle clear with a revolver, a rifle and a shotgun — every record kept between visits.

v1.11 — Shotguns reach farther and hit harder at mid range, their patterns still spreading wider with distance — and in bottle practice a pattern now breaks every bottle standing in its area. Rifles hit harder the longer the shot. Plus graphics quality in Settings — Low, Medium and High — and High renders the street at its finest: soft live shadows, rich golden light and dust in the air.

v1.10 — Shotgun patterns now spread with distance: tight and hard-hitting up close, opening wider the farther the shot flies — at long range most pellets miss and those that land hit weaker, in duels and bottle practice alike.

v1.9 — Inventory is now its own screen off the main menu — everything you own sorted neatly into Guns, Hats and Clothes, equipped gear marked, one tap to equip. The Store and the Inventory both have a clear Back button to the menu.

v1.8 — Low guns reload fast: a double barrel speed-loads both shells at once in one hand motion, and the single-shot Sharps drops its one round straight in. Six-guns and rifles still feed one round at a time — small capacity, fast reload; big capacity, slow reload.

v1.7 — Shotguns and rifles join the Store, held in both hands, with real balance: rifles reach and hit hard but draw slow, shotguns maul up close and scatter at range, six-guns draw fastest. New realistic hats, an Inventory tab for everything you own, store prices raised and the Store rebuilt clear — categories, plain prices, owned and equipped marked. The stray left hand is gone from the revolver view.

v1.6 — Practice bottles now stand in random spots every round — never the same layout twice — and the practice words sit low and fade clear, so they never cover the bottles.

v1.5 — Updates moved out of Learn to Play: tap the game version to open this short log. Learn to Play is just the rules now.

v1.4 — Practice is timed: the clock starts on your first shot and stops at the last bottle. Best time saved and shown in Practice.

v1.3 — Real recorded spaghetti-western music replaces the old synth tune. Toggle it in Settings.

v1.2 — Banner words no longer overlap the HUD, store gun finishes show their true colours in hand, and no gunman hides behind a pillar in the 3-man duel.

v1.1 — Settings added: music on/off and a real 30 / 60 / 120 FPS picker. No Learn tab on the way in.

v1.0.1 — Full screen with no black bars, cinematic camera stays inside the walls on both maps, and tap-through lands on the menu — never straight into a match.

v1.0 — Money and a wallet, the Store with finer guns and clothes, and a pre-match cinematic showing your equipped gear, with a real stance and idle motion.

v0.9 — Clean one-screen menu, round RELOAD button, no auto-reload, brighter practice bottles.

v0.8 — The Saloon duel map, plus bottle-shooting Practice mode.

v0.7 — Opponent's left hand hangs naturally, reload works in and after duels, and cover blocks shots honestly.

v0.6 — Hands rebuilt clean, slimmer holster, and the full revolver shows in the leather, on the draw and in aim.

v0.5 — No fire button: hold anywhere to aim. Gunmen start coming in company — two at once, then three in the final duel.

v0.4 — Hold at the bell and the iron snaps straight into aim-down-sights; let go early and it sprays wild from the hip.

v0.3 — Aim with the gun itself. No crosshair.

v0.2 — Ragdoll deaths, a more realistic six-shooter, and duels stretched out from 7 to 19 paces.

v0.1 — The first ride: six quick-draw duels on Main Street at golden hour. Wait for the bell — head or heart ends it.
